attempts.sql: SELECT c.symbol_id, COUNT(*)::INTEGER AS method_count FROM code.symbols c JOIN code.symbols m ON m.file_id = c.file_id AND m.kind = 'method' AND m.line_start > c.line_start AND m.line_end <= c.line_end JOIN code.files f ON f.file_id = c.file_id WHERE c.kind = 'class' AND f.is_test = false GROUP BY c.symbol_id HAVING COUNT(*) >= 20 ORDER BY method_count DESC, c.symbol_id ASC

request:
Which classes in the non-test code define at least 20 methods directly in their own body? Count every method definition separately (a property getter and its setter count as two; inherited methods and methods of nested classes do not count). Return each class's symbol ID and its method count, largest count first, ties broken by symbol ID alphabetically.

Requested output columns: symbol_id (string), method_count (integer). Order the rows as the question asks.
explanation: Joins each class symbol to method symbols in the same file whose line range falls within the class's line range, which captures methods defined directly in the class body (including property getters/setters) while excluding inherited and nested-class methods. Filters to non-test files and classes, groups by class symbol, and keeps those with at least 20 methods. Results are ordered by count descending then symbol ID.
sql: SELECT c.symbol_id, COUNT(*)::INTEGER AS method_count FROM code.symbols c JOIN code.symbols m ON m.file_id = c.file_id AND m.kind = 'method' AND m.line_start > c.line_start AND m.line_end <= c.line_end JOIN code.files f ON f.file_id = c.file_id WHERE c.kind = 'class' AND f.is_test = false GROUP BY c.symbol_id HAVING COUNT(*) >= 20 ORDER BY method_count DESC, c.symbol_id ASC
